purpose: Summative artwork applying A9.1, A9.2, A9.3, A9.4, A9.5, A9.7. Used as Lesson 5 capstone evidence.
student_learning_goal: I can use shapes to make a safari picture and describe it.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can use shapes to make a safari picture and describe it.
header.character_watermark: Sammy and Mira together in the top-right corner of the header, smiling at each other. Small (~1.5in tall combined). References both 'Sammy the Safari Sloth' and 'Mira the Map-Making Monkey' assets from blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Pick 5 shapes you will use in your safari picture. Write or draw them.
parts.visual_layout: A vertical plan list with 5 numbered slots stacked centred on the page. Each slot is wide enough (~3in) for the child to either write a shape name or sketch a small thumbnail. To the right of the list is a reference column showing all 10 shapes the child has learned: 5 2D outlines (circle, triangle, square, rectangle, hexagon) and 5 3D shaded shapes (sphere, cube, cylinder, cone, pyramid).

image_placeholders.description: A small two-column shape reference for a Kindergarten worksheet. Left column: 5 2D shape outlines stacked vertically (circle, triangle, square, rectangle, hexagon), each ~0.8in tall, B&W line art. Right column: 5 3D shaded shapes stacked vertically (sphere, cube, cylinder, cone, pyramid), each ~0.8in tall, with light shading. Names printed underneath each thumbnail. Suitable as an at-a-glance vocabulary reference.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P1_REFERENCE at Part 1: instructions ask the child to pick 5 shapes for their picture. The reference shows all learned shapes; keywords name examples of both 2D (circle, triangle, square) and 3D (sphere, cube) so the child can choose from a mix.

parts.answer_key: Any 5 shape names or thumbnails. Accept any combination of 2D and 3D shapes from the reference. Strongest plans mix 2D and 3D and include at least one of each category.

parts.student_instructions: Use your plan to draw a safari picture. Compose at least 1 bigger shape from smaller shapes.
parts.visual_layout: A large blank picture frame centred on the page (~6in × 5in) with a thin border. Below the frame, a small instruction reminder strip: 'Use 5+ shapes. Compose at least 1 bigger shape.' To the right of the frame, a small Sammy thumbnail giving a thumbs-up.

image_placeholders.description: A large blank picture frame ~6in × 5in for a Kindergarten safari capstone artwork. Thin solid border, no fill or content inside. To the right of the frame, a small thumbnail of Sammy the Safari Sloth giving a thumbs-up (~1in tall). Generous workspace for the child's creative artwork using shapes.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P2_FRAME at Part 2: instructions ask the child to build a safari picture using 5+ shapes including 1 composed shape. The frame provides the workspace; the keywords 'safari' and 'shapes' name the artwork's purpose. Sammy thumbnail reinforces the unit's anchor character.

parts.answer_key: Any safari-themed picture using 5+ shapes (2D or 3D) with at least one composed bigger shape (e.g., 2 triangles compose a giraffe head, 6 triangles compose a hexagonal sun). Strong responses mix 2D and 3D and use clear shape outlines that match the names from Part 1.

parts.student_instructions: Write 3 sentences about your picture using position words.
parts.visual_layout: Three sentence-frame rows stacked vertically. Each row reads 'The ___ is ___ the ___.' with three blanks (object — position word — reference object). To the right is a small position-word reference box listing: above, below, beside, inside, outside, between.

image_placeholders.description: Three sentence-frame response rows stacked vertically for a Kindergarten worksheet. Each row reads 'The ___ is ___ the ___.' with three clearly underlined blanks. Generous height between rows. To the right, a small reference box listing 6 position words in a vertical list: above, below, beside, inside, outside, between.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P3_FRAMES at Part 3: instructions ask the child to describe their picture using position words. The sentence frames give structured response slots; the position-word reference provides the vocabulary.

parts.answer_key: Any 3 valid sentences referencing the child's own picture. Examples: 'The sun is above the tree.' 'The lion is beside the rock.' 'The monkey is inside the cave.' Accept any sentence that uses a real picture element and a position word correctly.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, share your picture with a partner. Tell them what shapes you used and where everything is.
teacher_notes: Lesson 5 capstone — summative evidence for the unit. Score against the capstone rubric (provided in assessment_suite). Look for: 5+ different shapes used (A9.1, A9.2); at least 1 composed shape (A9.4); position-word descriptions (A9.3, A9.6); shape art application (A9.7). Children who completed all 3 parts independently demonstrate full unit mastery.
